text:
Maya: quick check — did the mixed-fleet priming runs finish? need a short cost+quality snapshot to feed GTN recommendation.
Sam: finished last night, uploaded raw logs/gists here: https://gist.github.com/redwood/mixed-fleet-3087 (summary below).
Jordan: awesome, just need the TL;DR numbers (unit cost delta, latency p95, and any longform quality regressions).
Sam: TL;DR: mixed-fleet = using nova7b-int6 for short-turns + orion14b-int6 fallback on long turns + light priming (avg +7% tokens). Results: 
```
baseline (opt13b-int8): unit_cost = $0.096 / 1k tokens, p95 = 320ms, longform QA F1 = 0.892
mixed-fleet: unit_cost = $0.061 / 1k tokens, p95 = 340ms, longform QA F1 = 0.882
priming tax: +7% tokens but +2.1% short-answer recall on search-style prompts
```
Tess: can you convert to per-100k tokens? product asks in that unit.
Sam: sure — per-100k tokens: baseline = $9.60, mixed-fleet = $6.10. Net savings ~= $3.50 / 100k tokens (36%).
Jordan: where is the quality hit concentrated? is it hallucination, missing facts, or style?
Sam: mostly thin on long-context synthesis (multi-paragraph summarization). single-turn Q/A and extraction are roughly parity. We measured a small drop on BLEU-like metrics on prompts >800 tokens.
Maya: product wants a routing recommendation and a safe rollout plan for GTN (they care >95% parity on longform).
Jordan: proposal: traffic split by input length + warmstart cache:
- short (<200 tokens): nova7b-int6 80% of short traffic (cheap), fallback to orion14b-int6 on low-confidence responses
- mid (200-800): route 60% nova, 40% orion
- long (>800): orion14b-int6 primary, nova as fast draft then re-roll if low confidence
Also enable KV warmstart for user hot buckets to reduce p95 on long multi-turn.
Sam: simulation shows combined policy yields ~30-38% cost reduction vs baseline while keeping longform F1 within 0.005 of baseline if we run a quick lightweight re-ranker (orion-lite rerank) on outputs flagged low-confidence.
Tess: what gating flags and metrics should GTN track?
Maya: create feature flag `priming.mixedfleet.v1`. Canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% with rollback on either:
- delta_unit_cost > -20% (i.e., if savings drop below expectation)
- longform_F1_drop > 0.01 absolute
- regen_rate increase > 1.5x or p95 latency > 500ms
Jordan: add automated sampling: send 0.1% of traffic to full-eval pipeline (human judgement + synthetic metrics) for the first 2 weeks.
Sam: I'll wire up the canary tomorrow. I left a small config snippet in the gist; paste here for quick reference:
```json
{
  "routing": [
    {"max_len": 200, "primary": "nova7b-int6", "fallback": "orion14b-int6", "weight_primary": 0.8},
    {"min_len": 201, "max_len": 800, "primary": "nova7b-int6", "fallback": "orion14b-int6", "weight_primary": 0.6},
    {"min_len": 801, "primary": "orion14b-int6", "fallback": "nova7b-int6", "weight_primary": 1.0}
  ],
  "priming": {"extra_tokens_pct": 7},
  "flags": ["priming.mixedfleet.v1"]
}
```
Maya: solid. also include a cheap reranker flow id `orion-lite-rerank` in the canary so we can validate quality cheaply.
Sam: added to the gist; I'll open a PR for ops tomorrow.
ops-bot: scheduled: canary rollout `priming.mixedfleet.v1` -> 5% at 3087654300, healthchecks enabled.
Tess: one more ask for GTN doc — capture expected amortized savings by endpoint shape (e.g., search vs summarization). can someone draft a tiny table?
Jordan: I'll draft an appendix: per-endpoint expected delta (search: -40% cost, summarization: -20% cost but risk of -0.008 F1).
Maya: perfect. let's aim to have the PR + GTN recommendation by EOD tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: will do. ping me if you want the raw slices.
Jordan: can we also add a small A/B that bumps priming from +7% to +10% to see recall vs token tradeoff? might be worth a microexperiment post-rollout.
Maya: yes, add `priming.mixedfleet.v1.priming_intensity` as a rollout knob (default 7%).
Sam: noted. closing loop on this thread and moving the docs into the GTN repo after PR.
Tess: ack.
Maya: thanks everyone.
